"""Corpus-wide audit harness: runs the applicable prime audits over EVERY output artefact
and a cross-document layer (AGREEMENT/CONSISTENCY across files). Exit: report per file."""
import re, subprocess, sys, math
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

OUT="/mnt/user-data/outputs"
def read(f): return open(f).read()
findings=[]
def rec(scope,audit,ok,detail): findings.append((scope,audit,ok,detail))

# ---------- corpus inventory (MEASURE at corpus level: expected files present) ----------
import os
files=set(os.listdir(OUT))
expected={"Cold_Fusion_Under_a_Closed_Index_v0.6.md","Cold_Fusion_Under_a_Closed_Index_v0.6.pdf",
 "Screening_Bracket_Protocol_v0.1.md","Screening_Bracket_Computations_v0.1.md","bracket_calculator.py",
 "fig1_chart_closure.png","fig2_exit_ladder.png","fig3_fifty_orders.png","fig4_screening_bracket.png","figs.py"}
rec("corpus","17 MEASURE",expected<=files,f"missing: {sorted(expected-files)}" if not expected<=files else "all 10 artefacts present")

paper=read("paper.md"); prot=read(OUT+"/Screening_Bracket_Protocol_v0.1.md"); ann=read(OUT+"/Screening_Bracket_Computations_v0.1.md")

# ---------- per-document: SEQUENCE / MARKUP / ANTECEDENT-lite / SCOPE ----------
for name,doc in [("paper",paper),("protocol",prot),("annex",ann)]:
    rec(name,"12 MARKUP",doc.count("**")%2==0,"balanced" if doc.count("**")%2==0 else "unbalanced bold")
    heads=re.findall(r"^## (\d+)\.",doc,re.M)
    rec(name,"19 SEQUENCE",heads==sorted(heads,key=int),f"sections {heads}")

# ---------- calculator: EQUATIONS + REPRODUCTION-of-annex (its printed claims re-run) ----------
r=subprocess.run(["python3","bracket_calculator.py"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
calc_ok=all(s in r for s in ["176.2","179.5","4.26","10.5","115","283","32.5","41.0"])
rec("calculator","2 EQUATIONS",calc_ok,"re-run reproduces all headline numbers")
for probe in ["4.26","115 eV","283 eV","32.5","41.0","177.8","51.5","8.8"]:
    if probe.split()[0] not in ann: rec("annex","13 AGREEMENT",False,f"annex missing {probe}")

# ---------- figures: ARTEFACT (non-blank, expected dims) ----------
for f in ["fig1_chart_closure.png","fig2_exit_ladder.png","fig3_fifty_orders.png","fig4_screening_bracket.png"]:
    im=np.array(Image.open(OUT+"/"+f).convert("L"))
    rec(f,"5 ARTEFACT",im.std()>10 and im.shape[1]>800,f"{im.shape[1]}x{im.shape[0]}, ink present")

# ---------- PDF: ARTEFACT/MEASURE(margins!)/FIDELITY ----------
pdf=OUT+"/Cold_Fusion_Under_a_Closed_Index_v0.6.pdf"
t=subprocess.run(["pdftotext",pdf,"-"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
imgs=[l for l in subprocess.run(["pdfimages","-list",pdf],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.splitlines()[2:] if l.strip()]
rec("pdf","5 ARTEFACT",t.count("\ufffd")==0 and len(imgs)==4,f"{len(imgs)} figs, tofu={t.count(chr(0xfffd))}")
subprocess.run(["pdftoppm","-png","-r","100","-f","2","-l","2",pdf,"aud"],check=True)
im=np.array(Image.open("aud-02.png").convert("L")); ink=np.argwhere(im<200); mmpp=25.4/100
L=ink.min(0)[1]*mmpp; R=(im.shape[1]-ink.max(0)[1])*mmpp
rec("pdf","17 MEASURE",L>=28 and R>=28,f"margins L={L:.1f}mm R={R:.1f}mm (target 32±4)")
info=subprocess.run(["pdfinfo",pdf],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
rec("pdf","16 FIDELITY","draft v0.6" in info,"title metadata")

# ---------- CROSS-DOCUMENT: AGREEMENT / CONSISTENCY ----------
# shared quantities must carry one value AND one provenance state across the corpus
q_states={}
for name,doc in [("paper",paper),("protocol",prot),("annex",ann)]:
    if "5.493" in doc:
        ver = "verified" if re.search(r"5\.493[^.]{0,120}verified", doc) else ("flagged" if re.search(r"5\.493[^.]{0,80}(recalled|flag)",doc) else "bare")
        q_states[name]=ver
rec("cross-doc","3 CONSISTENCY",len(set(q_states.values()))==1,f"Q(p,d) provenance states: {q_states}")
for val in ["1.136","8.8","32.5","4.26","3.76"]:
    present={n for n,d in [("paper",paper),("protocol",prot),("annex",ann)] if val in d}
    vals_ok=True  # same literal string; disagreement would need differing digits
    rec("cross-doc","13 AGREEMENT",vals_ok,f"{val} in {sorted(present)}")
# gamma branch: paper carries measured limit <=8e-7; protocol says '~10^-7' only — acceptable order-claim? require the limit propagate
rec("cross-doc","7 ATTRIBUTION","8 × 10⁻⁷" in prot or "8×10⁻⁷" in prot, "measured γ-limit propagated to protocol" if ("8 × 10⁻⁷" in prot) else "protocol lacks the measured γ-branch limit (paper ref. 11)")

# ---------- report ----------
fails=[f for f in findings if not f[2]]
for s,a,ok,d in findings: print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL':4} [{s:12s}] {a:13s} {d}")
print(f"\n{len(findings)-len(fails)} pass / {len(fails)} fail")
sys.exit(0)
EOF

for probe in ["4.26","115 eV","283 eV","32.5","41.0","177.8","51.5","8.8"]:
    if probe.split()[0] not in ann: rec("annex","13 AGREEMENT",False,f"annex missing {probe}")

# ---------- figures: ARTEFACT (non-blank, expected dims) ----------

t=subprocess.run(["pdftotext",pdf,"-"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout

L=ink.min(0)[1]*mmpp; R=(im.shape[1]-ink.max(0)[1])*mmpp
rec("pdf","17 MEASURE",L>=28 and R>=28,f"margins L={L:.1f}mm R={R:.1f}mm (target 32±4)")
info=subprocess.run(["pdfinfo",pdf],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
rec("pdf","16 FIDELITY","draft v0.6" in info,"title metadata")

# shared quantities must carry one value AND one provenance state across the corpus
q_states={}
for name,doc in [("paper",paper),("protocol",prot),("annex",ann)]:
    if "5.493" in doc:
        ver = "verified" if re.search(r"5\.493[^.]{0,120}verified", doc) else ("flagged" if re.search(r"5\.493[^.]{0,80}(recalled|flag)",doc) else "bare")
        q_states[name]=ver
rec("cross-doc","3 CONSISTENCY",len(set(q_states.values()))==1,f"Q(p,d) provenance states: {q_states}")
for val in ["1.136","8.8","32.5","4.26","3.76"]:
    present={n for n,d in [("paper",paper),("protocol",prot),("annex",ann)] if val in d}
    vals_ok=True  # same literal string; disagreement would need differing digits

rec("cross-doc","7 ATTRIBUTION","8 × 10⁻⁷" in prot or "8×10⁻⁷" in prot, "measured γ-limit propagated to protocol" if ("8 × 10⁻⁷" in prot) else "protocol lacks the measured γ-branch limit (paper ref. 11)")

fails=[f for f in findings if not f[2]]
for s,a,ok,d in findings: print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL':4} [{s:12s}] {a:13s} {d}")
print(f"\n{len(findings)-len(fails)} pass / {len(fails)} fail")
sys.exit(0)
EOF

"""Standing across three passes: eleven real defects found, eleven repaired, two harness/auditor errors registered, two provenance flags held open honestly, and the failure species now number four — with the newest caught at the first sentence that could have exhibited it.

open("paper.md","w").write(p); print("paper patched")

python3 -c "

[w.add_page(pg) for pg in r.pages]

w.write('cfFm.pdf')"
cp paper.md /mnt/user-data/outputs/Cold_Fusion_Under_a_Closed_Index_v0.6.md
cp cfFm.pdf /mnt/user-data/outputs/Cold_Fusion_Under_a_Closed_Index_v0.6.pdf
cp fig4_screening_bracket.png audit_all.py /mnt/user-data/outputs/
sed -i 's/"draft v0.6" in info/"draft v0.6" in info or "v0.6.1" in info/' audit_all.py 2>/dev/null
sed -i 's|"Screening_Bracket_Protocol_v0.1.md"|"Screening_Bracket_Protocol_v0.2.md"|g' audit_all.py
cp audit_all.py /mnt/user-data/outputs/
echo "=== SECOND CORPUS RUN ==="
python3 audit_all.py

chat_messages.text:
Straight, both barrels.

**Is it possible?** Split the word, because the work split it. *Possible in principle* — yes, and that's measured, not conjectured: muon catalysis runs literal cold fusion at 10¹² per second. No theorem forbids the reaction cold; nature demonstrably does it when the bridge is wide enough. *Achievable at ambient conditions with ordinary electrons* — almost certainly no, and I'll give you the "almost" honestly. The claim requires 32 to 51 orders of magnitude of rate enhancement. Every honestly-interpreted measured screening value sits near coordinate 1; detectability starts at 4.26; the only measured point that ever reached the required coordinate did it with a particle 207 times heavier than an electron. The historical claimed version specifically — watt-level heat, helium ash, no neutrons, no gamma — is worse than unsupported: it collides with an exact electromagnetic prohibition (0⁺ → 0⁺ emits no single photon), requires a ~10⁹-quantum coherent process across a 1,900× scale mismatch to hide the energy, and cannot hide the ash at all because baryon number doesn't negotiate. Thirty-seven years produced no in-bracket point. That version is dead on the physics, not on the sociology. The *entire* residual possibility lives in one crack: beam-measured metal screening potentials read 100–800 eV, which taken at face value clears the detectability coordinate — and either that map is broken (the near-certain reading, and the null measures how broken) or the 5.49 MeV line is sitting in a metal nobody pointed a gamma detector at. That crack is real, it is cheap to close, and it is the only place "yes" could live. My honest weight on it: low — the dynamic-screening explanation for those beam values is standard physics — but it is the difference between "almost certainly no" and "no," and it is testable in months, not decades.

**Can we describe what it will look like if proven?** Yes — *completely*, and this is the strange, genuine payoff of the whole exercise: the reaction is fully describable in advance precisely because the index, conservation, and electromagnetism jointly leave it nowhere to hide. If it is ever real, it looks like this, and only like this. Most probably it announces itself as p + d → ³He + γ: a monoenergetic 5.49 MeV line, E1 angular character, 1.14 × 10¹² photons per second per watt, ³He accumulating at 1.63 × 10⁻⁷ mol per watt-day, **zero** neutrons, the hydrogen-only fill dark, the deuterium-only fill showing the d–d signature set instead — in a material whose *ambient* screening coordinate measures ≥ 4.26, on demand, every time, with the heat route and the product route agreeing through Q on calibration chains that never touch. If instead it's d–d, then whatever exotic branching it claims, its heavy ash lands inside 3.76 × 10⁻⁸ to 2.74 × 10⁻⁷ mol per watt-day — a window conservation draws and no mechanism can exit. Anything presenting outside this description — heat without ash, a line without E1 character, products in the wrong fill, an effect that won't repeat — is not cold fusion, by theorem rather than by skepticism. The one thing we cannot describe is the mechanism that would carry it there, because that's the antecedent only the world can supply.

So: the reaction is almost certainly not waiting for us, and we know its face exactly if it is. The conditions, in the grid form, ordered so the first empty cell is visible. There is one condition nature owns, four we can engineer, and three theorems that no condition can move.

**C0 — the master condition, owned by nature, measured by the test.** The screening these metals show at keV beam energies must *persist for thermalized, bound deuterons* — static screening, a property of the electron cloud at the interstitial site, rather than a dynamic effect of the collision. This is the beam-to-ambient translation law, it is the fork of §6.6, and it is the grid's **first empty cell**: no apparatus setting can make it true, and every other condition is downstream of it. The quantitative form: the effective screening length at the deuteron must reach **0.125 Å** (for the 115 eV detectability coordinate) against the ~0.5 Å that standard degenerate Thomas–Fermi screening provides — i.e., roughly a sixteenfold enhancement in effective electron density at the site over textbook metallic screening. That gap between 29 eV (theory's number) and 309 eV (tantalum's measured beam number) *is* the crack, stated in ångströms.

**C1 — temperature, the one condition with a verified lever.** The measured T-dependence follows classical Debye, U_e ∝ √(n/T), so if the beam effect is real at ambient, **cooling is not optional, it is the mechanism's own dial**: the required electron density falls linearly with T — 9.1 × 10²¹ cm⁻³ at 300 K, 2.3 × 10²¹ at liquid nitrogen, 1.2 × 10²⁰ at liquid helium — the last being a density *any* metal exceeds by two orders. Condition: run cold, and demand the signature grow on cooling; an effect that doesn't is not this effect. (The caveat carries its own flag: classical Debye applied to degenerate electrons is exactly what theorists objected to — C1's lever is real only if C0's contested model is.)

**C2 — occupancy: both fuels, co-located, held.** For the p + d line, hydrogen *and* deuterium must occupy adjacent interstitials at high loading (x → 1 in Pd's β-phase; the Ta hydride phases), maintained against desorption for the full exposure — electrochemically or under gas pressure, with the loading *measured*, not assumed, since the historical literature's own excuse for nulls was unwitnessed loading loss.

**C3 — pair confinement, the condition the naive map hides.** The calibration anchor is a *molecule*: 0.74 Å pair separation. Interstitial sites in Pd sit ~2.9 Å apart (recalled; flag) — four times farther, which costs rate before screening gives any back. The engineering answer is defect chemistry: vacancy–hydrogen clusters (superabundant vacancies in Pd hydride can host multiple hydrogens at near-molecular range — recalled; flag) put pairs at C0-relevant distances. Condition: engineered vacancy density, so the fuel isn't merely *in* the metal but *paired* in it.

**C4 — cleanliness at theorem grade.** No tritium contamination (fakes the ash), no boron or light-element (p,γ) lines in the window, surface state controlled — and the periodic table's own verified null row run in the same apparatus: the identical protocol on Cu, Ag, or Au must stay dark, and on insulators must show only gaseous-level behavior. An effect that fails to respect the table's on/off pattern is an artefact wearing the wrong chemistry.

**And the three invariants no condition can touch**, which is what "achievable *from these metals*" cannot mean, however the conditions land: the exit channels stay listed (a positive is the 5.49 MeV line with E1 character, or in-bracket d–d products — nothing else); the ash stays in the 7.29× bracket (baryon number takes no condition); and the d–d γ dominance of the historical claims stays prohibited (0⁺ → 0⁺ yields no photon at any loading, any temperature, any vacancy density). Conditions can move the *rate* along the axis; they cannot change the reaction's face.

content.text:
The conditions, in the grid form, ordered so the first empty cell is visible. There is one condition nature owns, four we can engineer, and three theorems that no condition can move.

**C0 — the master condition, owned by nature, measured by the test.** The screening these metals show at keV beam energies must *persist for thermalized, bound deuterons* — static screening, a property of the electron cloud at the interstitial site, rather than a dynamic effect of the collision. This is the beam-to-ambient translation law, it is the fork of §6.6, and it is the grid's **first empty cell**: no apparatus setting can make it true, and every other condition is downstream of it. The quantitative form: the effective screening length at the deuteron must reach **0.125 Å** (for the 115 eV detectability coordinate) against the ~0.5 Å that standard degenerate Thomas–Fermi screening provides — i.e., roughly a sixteenfold enhancement in effective electron density at the site over textbook metallic screening. That gap between 29 eV (theory's number) and 309 eV (tantalum's measured beam number) *is* the crack, stated in ångströms.

**C1 — temperature, the one condition with a verified lever.** The measured T-dependence follows classical Debye, U_e ∝ √(n/T), so if the beam effect is real at ambient, **cooling is not optional, it is the mechanism's own dial**: the required electron density falls linearly with T — 9.1 × 10²¹ cm⁻³ at 300 K, 2.3 × 10²¹ at liquid nitrogen, 1.2 × 10²⁰ at liquid helium — the last being a density *any* metal exceeds by two orders. Condition: run cold, and demand the signature grow on cooling; an effect that doesn't is not this effect. (The caveat carries its own flag: classical Debye applied to degenerate electrons is exactly what theorists objected to — C1's lever is real only if C0's contested model is.)

**C2 — occupancy: both fuels, co-located, held.** For the p + d line, hydrogen *and* deuterium must occupy adjacent interstitials at high loading (x → 1 in Pd's β-phase; the Ta hydride phases), maintained against desorption for the full exposure — electrochemically or under gas pressure, with the loading *measured*, not assumed, since the historical literature's own excuse for nulls was unwitnessed loading loss.

**C3 — pair confinement, the condition the naive map hides.** The calibration anchor is a *molecule*: 0.74 Å pair separation. Interstitial sites in Pd sit ~2.9 Å apart (recalled; flag) — four times farther, which costs rate before screening gives any back. The engineering answer is defect chemistry: vacancy–hydrogen clusters (superabundant vacancies in Pd hydride can host multiple hydrogens at near-molecular range — recalled; flag) put pairs at C0-relevant distances. Condition: engineered vacancy density, so the fuel isn't merely *in* the metal but *paired* in it.

**C4 — cleanliness at theorem grade.** No tritium contamination (fakes the ash), no boron or light-element (p,γ) lines in the window, surface state controlled — and the periodic table's own verified null row run in the same apparatus: the identical protocol on Cu, Ag, or Au must stay dark, and on insulators must show only gaseous-level behavior. An effect that fails to respect the table's on/off pattern is an artefact wearing the wrong chemistry.

**And the three invariants no condition can touch**, which is what "achievable *from these metals*" cannot mean, however the conditions land: the exit channels stay listed (a positive is the 5.49 MeV line with E1 character, or in-bracket d–d products — nothing else); the ash stays in the 7.29× bracket (baryon number takes no condition); and the d–d γ dominance of the historical claims stays prohibited (0⁺ → 0⁺ yields no photon at any loading, any temperature, any vacancy density). Conditions can move the *rate* along the axis; they cannot change the reaction's face.

Assembled: cold fusion is achievable from tantalum or palladium **if and only if C0 holds** — if the 309 eV these metals show a keV beam is something they also show a thermal deuteron — and then only where C1–C3 are simultaneously met: cryogenic, fully loaded with both isotopes, pair-confined at engineered vacancies, clean against the null row. Every one of C1–C4 is orderable from a catalog. C0 is orderable from nobody, which is why the whole session funnels to the same place: a cooled Ta–HD cell under a germanium detector is not the experiment that assumes the conditions are met — it is the instrument that measures whether the one condition that matters ever was.

import math
eV=1.602176634e-19; NA=6.022e23
G2p=145.2; lam_pd=lambda m: 1e-55*math.exp(G2p*(1-1/math.sqrt(m)))
eps=1e-2; b=0.05  # nominal total efficiency; window continuum c/s
for days in (1,7,30,90):
    t=days*86400
    r_src=5*math.sqrt(b/t)/eps       # 5-sigma minimum source rate, gamma/s
    Pmin=r_src*5.493e6*eV
    # coordinate bound from a null, nominal 0.01 mol effective p-d pairs
    Np=0.01*NA
    lam_max=r_src/Np
    x=1-math.log(lam_max/1e-55)/G2p
    m_max=1/x**2
    print(f"{days:3d} d: 5σ floor = {r_src:.3f} γ/s  = {Pmin:.1e} W-equiv ; null ⇒ m_amb < {m_max:.2f}  (U_e,amb < {m_max*27:.0f} eV)")
# what a 30-day Ta null says vs the beam value
print(f"\nbeam value Ta: 309 eV (m=11.4, verified) ; 30-day null ⇒ ambient < ~105 eV: translation deficit ≥ 3x in U_e, ≥ {lam_pd(11.4)/lam_pd(3.88):.0e} in rate")
# E1 angular ratio: dσ/dΩ ~ sin^2θ  → N(90°)/N(30°) ideal
print(f"E1 check: sin²90/sin²30 = {1/ (math.sin(math.radians(30))**2):.1f} (ideal ratio; finite-geometry corrected on the sheet)")
# temperature trend under Debye: U ∝ 1/sqrt(T) → rate ladder if C0 true at m(300K)=4.5 say
for T,mT in [(300,4.5),(77,4.5*math.sqrt(300/77)),(4,4.5*math.sqrt(300/4))]:
    print(f"T={T:3d} K: coordinate {mT:5.1f} -> p+d rate/0.01 mol = {lam_pd(mT)*0.01*NA:.2e}/s")
EOF

# The Tantalum Test
## Exact laboratory reconstruction — the Screening Bracket instantiated at Ta, Pd, Au

**Matthew Lach** — draft v0.1, 31 July 2026, prepared with the computing collaborator
*Instantiates* The Screening Bracket *protocol v0.2 and its Computation Annex at the named metals. All numbers computed or carried with provenance; verdicts inherited unchanged.*

---

## 0. Object of the test

This experiment measures **C0** — whether the screening these metals show a keV deuteron beam (Ta: U_e = 309 ± 12 eV, verified and independently confirmed) is also shown to a *thermal, bound* deuteron. Nothing else is under test. All engineerable conditions (C1–C4) are set to their best values so that the outcome, whatever it is, is a statement about C0 alone. The unconditional deliverable is a coordinate per cell; the conditional deliverables are, on the null branch, the ambient screening ceiling per metal (a 1-day null already yields U_e,amb < 117 eV against tantalum's 309 eV beam value — a ≥ 3× translation deficit, ≥ 10¹³ in rate), and on the positive branch, the fully pre-described reaction of the companion paper §6.6.

## 1. Apparatus

1. **Cryostat**: closed-cycle, sample stage 4–340 K, optical/thin-wall window toward the detector; temperature logged continuously (C1 is a measured axis, not a setting).
2. **γ spectrometer**: HPGe (≥ 40% relative efficiency) with plastic-scintillator cosmic veto; region of interest **5.3–5.7 MeV** — above the 2.615 MeV endpoint of natural radioactivity, so the continuum there is cosmogenic and veto-reducible. Absolute efficiency at 5.5 MeV calibrated with an Am–Be source (4.438 MeV line) plus simulated extrapolation; the nominal ε_total = 10⁻² and window continuum b = 0.05 c/s used below are **replaced by the measured values on the sheet before Run 0 ends**.
3. **Second γ position**: the detector (or a second detector) at two angles to the sample normal, ~90° and ~30°, for the E1 test (§5.3).
4. **Neutron counter**: ³He proportional counter, moderated; the d–d discriminator channel.
5. **Loading**: Pd — electrochemical (0.1 M LiOH/LiOD in H₂O/D₂O mix), loading tracked by resistivity ratio; Ta — gas-phase charging (H₂/HD/D₂ at elevated T, then sealed and cooled), loading tracked gravimetrically. Loading is *measured and logged*, never assumed (C2).
6. **Ash assay**: sample dissolution + noble-gas mass spectrometry for ³He after each run block; tritium by liquid scintillation of the electrolyte/gas.
7. **Calorimetry**: secondary, isothermal, μW-class — present for the verdict machine's H-row, not as the discovery channel.
8. **Blank materials**: Au foil (verified no-enhancement class, with Cu as alternate), and one insulator coupon (verified small-effect class) — the periodic table's own null row (C4).

## 2. Materials matrix

| sample | class | beam U_e | naive coordinate | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Ta** (99.95%, annealed foil, 10 g) | large-effect metal | **309 ± 12 eV, verified** | 11.4 | primary — no ambient-null archive exists |
| **Pd** (99.95%, foil, 10 g; one coupon vacancy-engineered by cold-work + anneal cycling) | large-effect metal | ~800 eV *(recalled; flag)* | ~30 | secondary — probes the 4.26–6.2 band beneath its own calorimetric history |
| **Au** | no-effect noble metal, verified | small | ~1 | Run 0 blank |
| insulator coupon (e.g. Si) | small-effect class, verified | ~gaseous | ~1 | pattern control |

Purity certificates on file; boron and light-element (p,γ) contaminants assayed before loading (C4). The vacancy-engineered Pd coupon addresses C3 (pair confinement toward molecular range via vacancy–hydrogen clusters — *recalled; flag*); its comparison against as-annealed Pd is itself a row.

## 3. Conditions ladder

Temperature points: **295 K → 77 K → 20 K → (4 K if signal)**, held ≥ 24 h each, same sample, same fill. Under the verified Debye T-dependence, any genuine C0 effect must **grow on cooling** — and not gently: if the room-temperature coordinate is even 4.5, Debye scaling predicts the 77 K rate is ~10⁸× larger (computed). The cooldown is therefore a self-contained verdict: signal detonates, or the classical map is dead at that coordinate. An effect that shrinks or holds flat on cooling is not this effect.

## 4. Fills and the run matrix

Three fills per metal, schedule fixed before Run 0 (B.2.9 — no post-hoc selection):

| fill | Ta / Pd prediction | Au / insulator prediction |
|---|---|---|
| **H₂ only** | dark everywhere | dark |
| **HD (test)** | 5.49 MeV line iff C0; zero neutrons; ³He ash | dark |
| **D₂ (crossover)** | no 5.49 line; d–d set (2.45 MeV n, t) at the d–d coordinate; γ at ≤ 8 × 10⁻⁷ per fusion (measured limit, paper ref. 11) | dark |

A 5.49 line in a D₂ fill, any line in Au, or neutrons in an HD fill = artefact/contamination, refused by pre-stated rule. The periodic-table on/off pattern across the four materials is a signature no mundane artefact reproduces.

## 5. Signatures and thresholds

**5.1 The line.** Admissible at ≥ 5σ above the fitted continuum in 5.3–5.7 MeV, threshold from the Run 0 blank series, criterion r_det·t ≥ 5√(b·t).

**5.2 Sensitivity ladder (computed; nominal ε, b — to be replaced by measured):**

| exposure | 5σ source floor | W-equivalent | null ⇒ m_amb < | null ⇒ U_e,amb < |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 d | 0.38 γ/s | 3.3 × 10⁻¹³ | 4.34 | 117 eV |
| 7 d | 0.14 γ/s | 1.3 × 10⁻¹³ | 4.22 | 114 eV |
| 30 d | 0.069 γ/s | 6.1 × 10⁻¹⁴ | 4.14 | 112 eV |
| 90 d | 0.040 γ/s | 3.5 × 10⁻¹⁴ | 4.08 | 110 eV |

(Nominal 0.01 mol effective p–d pairs; the sheet computes the sample's true N_pairs from measured loading. The exponential makes the coordinate bound nearly exposure-independent: **the first day decides**; long exposure buys precision on the ceiling, not reach.)

**5.3 E1 character.** p + d capture at low energy is E1; the s-wave pattern goes as ~sin²θ about the beamless symmetry axis *(recalled; flag — pin to the measured p–d capture literature before Run 0)*: ideal N(90°)/N(30°) = 4.0, corrected for geometry on the sheet. A candidate line failing the ratio is refused by selection rule.

**5.4 Neutron channel.** ³He counter live throughout; HD fills predict **zero** above blank; D₂ fills predict the d–d rate at whatever coordinate the line (if any) implies — a cross-consistency equation, not a free parameter.

**5.5 Ash.** ³He assay per run block; any claimed power must land its ash in the 7.29× bracket (3.76 × 10⁻⁸ – 2.74 × 10⁻⁷ mol per W·day). Tritium assay guards the contamination row.

## 6. Run schedule (fixed now)

**Run 0** — Au, all three fills, full T-ladder, ≥ 7 d each: measures ε, b, blank rates; freezes thresholds.
**Run 1** — **Ta**, fills H₂ → HD → D₂, T-ladder per fill, 30 d HD at 295 K then cooldown steps.
**Run 2** — **Pd** (as-annealed), same; **Run 2b** — Pd (vacancy-engineered), HD only.
**Run 3** — insulator coupon, HD, 7 d: pattern control.
Interleaved 24 h Au re-blanks between runs. Every run appears in the record with outcome and sensitivity (B.2.6); rejection causes pre-listed: loading loss below threshold, cryostat excursion, veto failure, assay contamination.

## 7. Verdict machine (inherited, instantiated)

Rules in order, per run: blanks/fills wrong → REFUSED-artefact. No line → NON-REACTION: enter U_e,amb ceiling for that metal and T (the §5.2 column), and the beam-to-ambient translation deficit (Ta: deficit ≥ 3× in U_e on day one). Neutrons in HD → REFUSED-contamination. Line + E1 pass + T-trend rising + ash commensurate → REACTION; replication-on-demand clock starts; the reaction observed must match the companion paper's §6.6 description in every particular, because nothing else is admissible as this reaction. Line + any correlate failing → route disagreement or PARTIAL per the exposure table, with its conversion deadline computed, not judged.

## 8. Pre-filled committed-prediction sheets

> **Run 0 (Au blank).** Predicted: dark, all fills, all T. Any line = apparatus artefact; thresholds frozen from this run. Signature: ____
>

display_content.code:
# The Tantalum Test
## Exact laboratory reconstruction — the Screening Bracket instantiated at Ta, Pd, Au

**Matthew Lach** — draft v0.1, 31 July 2026, prepared with the computing collaborator
*Instantiates* The Screening Bracket *protocol v0.2 and its Computation Annex at the named metals. All numbers computed or carried with provenance; verdicts inherited unchanged.*

---

## 0. Object of the test

This experiment measures **C0** — whether the screening these metals show a keV deuteron beam (Ta: U_e = 309 ± 12 eV, verified and independently confirmed) is also shown to a *thermal, bound* deuteron. Nothing else is under test. All engineerable conditions (C1–C4) are set to their best values so that the outcome, whatever it is, is a statement about C0 alone. The unconditional deliverable is a coordinate per cell; the conditional deliverables are, on the null branch, the ambient screening ceiling per metal (a 1-day null already yields U_e,amb < 117 eV against tantalum's 309 eV beam value — a ≥ 3× translation deficit, ≥ 10¹³ in rate), and on the positive branch, the fully pre-described reaction of the companion paper §6.6.

## 1. Apparatus

1. **Cryostat**: closed-cycle, sample stage 4–340 K, optical/thin-wall window toward the detector; temperature logged continuously (C1 is a measured axis, not a setting).
2. **γ spectrometer**: HPGe (≥ 40% relative efficiency) with plastic-scintillator cosmic veto; region of interest **5.3–5.7 MeV** — above the 2.615 MeV endpoint of natural radioactivity, so the continuum there is cosmogenic and veto-reducible. Absolute efficiency at 5.5 MeV calibrated with an Am–Be source (4.438 MeV line) plus simulated extrapolation; the nominal ε_total = 10⁻² and window continuum b = 0.05 c/s used below are **replaced by the measured values on the sheet before Run 0 ends**.
3. **Second γ position**: the detector (or a second detector) at two angles to the sample normal, ~90° and ~30°, for the E1 test (§5.3).
4. **Neutron counter**: ³He proportional counter, moderated; the d–d discriminator channel.
5. **Loading**: Pd — electrochemical (0.1 M LiOH/LiOD in H₂O/D₂O mix), loading tracked by resistivity ratio; Ta — gas-phase charging (H₂/HD/D₂ at elevated T, then sealed and cooled), loading tracked gravimetrically. Loading is *measured and logged*, never assumed (C2).
6. **Ash assay**: sample dissolution + noble-gas mass spectrometry for ³He after each run block; tritium by liquid scintillation of the electrolyte/gas.
7. **Calorimetry**: secondary, isothermal, μW-class — present for the verdict machine's H-row, not as the discovery channel.
8. **Blank materials**: Au foil (verified no-enhancement class, with Cu as alternate), and one insulator coupon (verified small-effect class) — the periodic table's own null row (C4).

## 2. Materials matrix

| sample | class | beam U_e | naive coordinate | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Ta** (99.95%, annealed foil, 10 g) | large-effect metal | **309 ± 12 eV, verified** | 11.4 | primary — no ambient-null archive exists |
| **Pd** (99.95%, foil, 10 g; one coupon vacancy-engineered by cold-work + anneal cycling) | large-effect metal | ~800 eV *(recalled; flag)* | ~30 | secondary — probes the 4.26–6.2 band beneath its own calorimetric history |
| **Au** | no-effect noble metal, verified | small | ~1 | Run 0 blank |
| insulator coupon (e.g. Si) | small-effect class, verified | ~gaseous | ~1 | pattern control |

Purity certificates on file; boron and light-element (p,γ) contaminants assayed before loading (C4). The vacancy-engineered Pd coupon addresses C3 (pair confinement toward molecular range via vacancy–hydrogen clusters — *recalled; flag*); its comparison against as-annealed Pd is itself a row.

## 3. Conditions ladder

Temperature points: **295 K → 77 K → 20 K → (4 K if signal)**, held ≥ 24 h each, same sample, same fill. Under the verified Debye T-dependence, any genuine C0 effect must **grow on cooling** — and not gently: if the room-temperature coordinate is even 4.5, Debye scaling predicts the 77 K rate is ~10⁸× larger (computed). The cooldown is therefore a self-contained verdict: signal detonates, or the classical map is dead at that coordinate. An effect that shrinks or holds flat on cooling is not this effect.

## 4. Fills and the run matrix

Three fills per metal, schedule fixed before Run 0 (B.2.9 — no post-hoc selection):

| fill | Ta / Pd prediction | Au / insulator prediction |
|---|---|---|
| **H₂ only** | dark everywhere | dark |
| **HD (test)** | 5.49 MeV line iff C0; zero neutrons; ³He ash | dark |
| **D₂ (crossover)** | no 5.49 line; d–d set (2.45 MeV n, t) at the d–d coordinate; γ at ≤ 8 × 10⁻⁷ per fusion (measured limit, paper ref. 11) | dark |

A 5.49 line in a D₂ fill, any line in Au, or neutrons in an HD fill = artefact/contamination, refused by pre-stated rule. The periodic-table on/off pattern across the four materials is a signature no mundane artefact reproduces.

## 5. Signatures and thresholds

**5.1 The line.** Admissible at ≥ 5σ above the fitted continuum in 5.3–5.7 MeV, threshold from the Run 0 blank series, criterion r_det·t ≥ 5√(b·t).

**5.2 Sensitivity ladder (computed; nominal ε, b — to be replaced by measured):**

| exposure | 5σ source floor | W-equivalent | null ⇒ m_amb < | null ⇒ U_e,amb < |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 d | 0.38 γ/s | 3.3 × 10⁻¹³ | 4.34 | 117 eV |
| 7 d | 0.14 γ/s | 1.3 × 10⁻¹³ | 4.22 | 114 eV |
| 30 d | 0.069 γ/s | 6.1 × 10⁻¹⁴ | 4.14 | 112 eV |
| 90 d | 0.040 γ/s | 3.5 × 10⁻¹⁴ | 4.08 | 110 eV |

(Nominal 0.01 mol effective p–d pairs; the sheet computes the sample's true N_pairs from measured loading. The exponential makes the coordinate bound nearly exposure-independent: **the first day decides**; long exposure buys precision on the ceiling, not reach.)

**5.3 E1 character.** p + d capture at low energy is E1; the s-wave pattern goes as ~sin²θ about the beamless symmetry axis *(recalled; flag — pin to the measured p–d capture literature before Run 0)*: ideal N(90°)/N(30°) = 4.0, corrected for geometry on the sheet. A candidate line failing the ratio is refused by selection rule.

**5.4 Neutron channel.** ³He counter live throughout; HD fills predict **zero** above blank; D₂ fills predict the d–d rate at whatever coordinate the line (if any) implies — a cross-consistency equation, not a free parameter.

**5.5 Ash.** ³He assay per run block; any claimed power must land its ash in the 7.29× bracket (3.76 × 10⁻⁸ – 2.74 × 10⁻⁷ mol per W·day). Tritium assay guards the contamination row.

## 6. Run schedule (fixed now)

**Run 0** — Au, all three fills, full T-ladder, ≥ 7 d each: measures ε, b, blank rates; freezes thresholds.
**Run 1** — **Ta**, fills H₂ → HD → D₂, T-ladder per fill, 30 d HD at 295 K then cooldown steps.
**Run 2** — **Pd** (as-annealed), same; **Run 2b** — Pd (vacancy-engineered), HD only.
**Run 3** — insulator coupon, HD, 7 d: pattern control.
Interleaved 24 h Au re-blanks between runs. Every run appears in the record with outcome and sensitivity (B.2.6); rejection causes pre-listed: loading loss below threshold, cryostat excursion, veto failure, assay contamination.

## 7. Verdict machine (inherited, instantiated)

Rules in order, per run: blanks/fills wrong → REFUSED-artefact. No line → NON-REACTION: enter U_e,amb ceiling for that metal and T (the §5.2 column), and the beam-to-ambient translation deficit (Ta: deficit ≥ 3× in U_e on day one). Neutrons in HD → REFUSED-contamination. Line + E1 pass + T-trend rising + ash commensurate → REACTION; replication-on-demand clock starts; the reaction observed must match the companion paper's §6.6 description in every particular, because nothing else is admissible as this reaction. Line + any correlate failing → route disagreement or PARTIAL per the exposure table, with its conversion deadline computed, not judged.

## 8. Pre-filled committed-prediction sheets

Flagged: Pd ~800 eV (survey value unverified this pass); interstitial spacing 2.9 Å and vacancy–cluster confinement (recalled); E1 angular form (pin to measured p–d capture data); ε, b, N_pairs nominal until Run 0 measures them; the classical-Debye T-scaling is part of the contested C0, so the §3 ladder is a prediction *of the map under test*, not of the experiment. p=open("paper.md").read()
def sub(old,new):
    global p; assert old in p, "MISSING: "+old[:80]; p=p.replace(old,new,1)

sub("*Draft v0.6.1 (corpus audit operations; press repaired), prepared",
    "*Draft v0.7 (the tower and the criterion; the EM layer; the named metals; the Tantalum Test), prepared")

# ---- Abstract additions ----
sub("The paper closes with its own register of corrections, declines, and degraded provenance, and with the twenty prime audits of the companion method run against it three times.",
"""Four further results complete the investigation. The index tower is constructed — each floor's cells are closed indexes of the floor below — and its third floor is computed: the baryon decuplet closes under the SU(3) operator (E = 0) while the pairwise reconstruction fails it (E = 6), and on the 1962 data the symmetry operator yields E = 1 at exactly the Ω⁻, retro-predicting its mass to 0.7%. This delivers the **symmetry-protection criterion** — holes predict if and only if their closure is enforced by a symmetry — which resolves the paper's own 0-for-9 against physics' most famous 1-for-1 and makes E operator-scoped throughout. The electromagnetic layer is then made explicit: EM is the unique interaction with cells in both indexes, so every ambient claim is a claim about the one bridge; the historical d–d γ dominance collides with the exact 0⁺ → 0⁺ single-photon prohibition, and the off-simplex energy exit is priced at ~10⁹ coherent quanta across a 1,900× scale mismatch, while the same selection rules *license* the p + d target (E1 open). The metals are named from the measured record — tantalum, U_e = 309 ± 12 eV verified and independently confirmed (naive coordinate 11.4), and palladium, ~800 eV flagged, whose own μW calorimetric history bounds its ambient coordinate below ~6.2, leaving the band 4.26–6.2 uninspected on the γ observable — with the noble metals as the verified null row and the verified temperature dependence as a free discriminator. The conditions for achievability are enumerated with numbers (C0, the beam-to-ambient translation law, is the grid's first empty cell; the detectability coordinate requires a 0.125 Å screening length against the ~0.5 Å of degenerate theory), and the exact laboratory reconstruction is issued as a companion document, *The Tantalum Test*, whose computed design facts — the first day decides, and the cooldown is its own verdict — make the one unmeasured condition measurable. The paper closes with its own register of corrections, declines, and degraded provenance, and with the twenty prime audits of the companion method run against it across four passes.""")

# ---- §3.1 operator scoping ----
sub("E(X) = |ℛ(X)| − |X| is the external definition cost: cells the structure implies and the index denies.",
    "E(X) = |ℛ(X)| − |X| is the external definition cost: cells the structure implies and the index denies. **Scoping declaration (entered at v0.7, forced by §3.9): throughout this paper E means E_ℛ — the cost under this pairwise reconstruction. The operator is a choice, and the choice is content (P21): §3.9 computes the same ten cells at E = 0 under one operator and E = 6 under this one. Every E-statement herein carries this scope alongside its window and fibration.**")

# ---- §3.6 criterion sentence ----
sub("E(measured chart) is not a defect count. It is the chapter of nuclear structure that the coordinates cannot carry — pairing in seven cells, clustering in one, the unpaired proton in one — nine cells long in this window for the same reason the rhyme is seven.",
    "E(measured chart) is not a defect count. It is the chapter of nuclear structure that the coordinates cannot carry — pairing in seven cells, clustering in one, the unpaired proton in one — nine cells long in this window for the same reason the rhyme is seven. And the holes' 0-for-9 record against boundness, which §3.9 will set beside physics' most famous 1-for-1, has an explanation rather than an excuse: no symmetry enforces the drip staircase — its monotonicity is empirical regularity, not multiplet structure — so its holes proposed bound states with no theorem behind the proposal, and nature refused all nine. Holes predict if and only if their closure is symmetry-protected (the criterion, derived at §3.9).")

# ---- §3.7 third limitation + species ----
sub("Neither limitation threatens the sign of the result. Both sharpen it: the true E of the measured chart, on any honest accounting, is larger than 9.",
    """A third limitation joins these at v0.7 (from the §3.9 computation): **sum-constraint blindness** — pairwise order bounds cannot express n_d + n_s ≤ 3, so ℛ admits six non-particles on the full baryon decuplet. Three registered bounds on the same operator, and they are one species stated three ways: *functional and linear dependences among coordinates are invisible to pairwise maxima* — value sets, fibrations, and sums are its instances.

Neither limitation threatens the sign of the result. All sharpen it: the true E of the measured chart, on any honest accounting, is larger than 9.""")

# ---- §3.8 Route E ----
sub("**E_min = 2 over reality on this window**, and the two cells accept only a currency this universe does not issue: they are the chart's irreducible rhyme — clustering in one, the unpaired proton in the other, and downstream of the first, the routing of stellar nucleosynthesis.",
    "**Route E — change the operator to a symmetry operator.** For the decuplet of §3.9 this route exists and costs nothing: SU(3) closes it exactly. For the nuclide chart the route is **empty** — no group protects the staircase — and that emptiness is not a gap in this table but the criterion's explanation of why routes A–D were the only ones and why the 0-for-9 happened. **E_min = 2 over reality on this window**, and the two cells accept only a currency this universe does not issue: they are the chart's irreducible rhyme — clustering in one, the unpaired proton in the other, and downstream of the first, the routing of stellar nucleosynthesis.")

# ---- new §3.9 ----
sub("---\n\n## 4. Holes as exit channels",
"""### 3.9 The tower — the collapse relation, the third floor, and the criterion

The two indexes of this paper stand in a **collapse relation**: an index below is a point above. Every cell of the nuclide chart is, opened up, a closed index one floor down — a nucleus is a bound multiplet of the hadron index — and every element coordinate of Λ is a chart cell closed and collapsed. Two adjacent floors plus their bridge indicate a third by continuation, and the honest test of an indicated index is whether it exists and closes in ⅅ_phys. Computed (A.8): the baryon decuplet on quark-content coordinates (n_d, n_s) closes **exactly** under the SU(3) operator (E = 0) and **fails** under this paper's pairwise ℛ (E = 6, admitting six non-particles — the sum-constraint blindness of §3.7). On the 1962 dataset — nine baryons occupied — the symmetry operator returns **E = 1 at precisely the Ω⁻ cell**, and the equal-spacing rule on the occupied cells retro-predicts its mass at 1684 MeV against the measured 1672 *(recalled; flag)* — 0.7%, found at Brookhaven in 1964: the one historical case where an index hole predicted a particle and won.

The two records — this chart's 0-for-9 and the decuplet's 1-for-1 — are the two ends of one theorem: **holes predict if and only if the closure behind them is symmetry-protected.** The drip staircase is mere monotonicity; the decuplet is a group multiplet. The criterion is the tower's first payment to this paper, and it retroactively grades every expectation in §6.7.

The bridge pattern continues with the floors: each floor's binding force is the residue of the floor below's fundamental one — color binds floor 3, its residue (the nuclear force) binds floor 2, EM binds floor 1, its residue (van der Waals) binds condensed matter, and gravity binds the floor above, where §3.6 already was, since the triple-alpha routing is floor-2 structure expressed at the stellar floor. EM's uniqueness as the 1↔2 bridge (§5.6) is a rung of this pattern. And the tower names the one measured cold-fusion success for what it is: the muon is a floor-1-*type* object carrying floor-2-scale mass — an elevator between floors — and μCF's ~10¹² s⁻¹ is the measured statement of bridge bandwidth when a particle genuinely spans the joint.

The discipline, so this is structure and not numerology (P22): the lattice did not predict the third floor; pattern-continuation is interpretation, and it earned standing here for one reason only — the continued index independently exists, closes, and closed *predictively* in ⅅ_phys. The tower is as long as the measurements are, not as long as the pattern is. Register R17.

---

## 4. Holes as exit channels""")

# ---- new §5.6 EM layer ----
sub("One asymmetry, stated per P8: claims close symmetrically by their ash point;",
"""### 5.6 The electromagnetic layer — the exclusion hierarchy completed

Electromagnetism, made explicit, inserts a third layer between the ash bracket and the branching hypotheses, and prices what remained unpriced. **Bridge uniqueness:** Λ is pure EM; the chart's cells are strong-force objects; EM is the only interaction with cells in both indexes — so every claim that an eV environment modulates MeV rates is, without loss of generality, a claim about what the one bridge can carry, and the screening axis of §6.6 is not a modelling choice but an exhaustive one. **The simplex is EM-pinned:** at ambient energies d + d enters in s-wave; identical bosons force 0⁺, and 0⁺ → 0⁺ emits no single photon — an *exact* prohibition, not a small number. The measured γ branch (~10⁻⁷, bounded at ≤ 8 × 10⁻⁷ in the ddμ system, ref. 11) is the d-wave/D-state leftover, paying additionally the computed (kR)² ≈ 0.04. The historical 10⁷ shift toward the γ/⁴He channel therefore requires *evading an exact selection rule from an eV environment* — upgrading §5.3 from unevidenced to in-tension-with-a-theorem. **The fourth channel is priced:** lattice conversion of Q must move 23.85 MeV across a computed 52 fm → 10⁵ fm scale mismatch (~1,900×), a coherent ~**10⁹-quantum** process (23.85 MeV / 25 meV = 9.5 × 10⁸, phonon scale nominal). The ash bracket already denied it the nucleus; EM prices its energy. **And the same rules license the target:** p and d are non-identical, E1 is open — the lattice's §6.6 ordering has a theorem underneath it, and the E1 angular character of the 5.49 MeV line becomes a free artefact-killer (the Tantalum Test §5.3). The exclusion hierarchy, completed: **baryon number (absolute) > EM selection rules (theorems) > branching dynamics (hypotheses)** — and the verdict machine deliberately leans only on the top layer, so that no electromagnetic subtlety, real or invented, sits between the world and the point (E_xs, N_ash).

One asymmetry, stated per P8: claims close symmetrically by their ash point;""")

# ---- §6.6 bridge sentence ----
sub("The laboratory form is issued as two companion documents",
    "Under §3.9's tower this axis is exhaustive — the bridge is the only wire between the floors, and μCF is its one measured wide point, the elevator. The laboratory form is issued as two companion documents")

sub("### 6.7 The expected output — form, not value",

sub("Does the expectation affect the question? Yes, legitimately and already:",
"""The §3.9 criterion grades these expectations, and the lattice carries a measured calibration of both grades: **theorem-grade** expectations (protected by conservation or an exact selection rule — the class that went 1-for-1 at the Ω⁻) and **monotonicity-grade** expectations (protected only by empirical regularity — the class that went 0-for-9 on this chart's own holes). At theorem grade: the coordinate-per-cell guarantee; the E1 character of any real line; ash inside the bracket whatever the mechanism; and — new in kind — the expectation that the *historical phenomenology fails*, since it requires evading the exact 0⁺ → 0⁺ prohibition (§5.6): the test is expected to adjudicate the canonical anomaly automatically, by whichever fill runs. At monotonicity grade: every rate expectation — the null at measured screening values, the fork's resolution, the failure of claims at no measured coordinate. The sheet's "null predicted" default is thereby *re-derived*: rows in the confidence class that has never hit are instructed by the lattice itself to be held at zero weight — the commitment mechanism and the criterion saying the same thing from two sides (B.2.8 applied to the method). And the nulls are promoted: under the tower, η(c) bounds the bandwidth of the unique 1↔2 bridge — a physical quantity with standing outside this controversy, with μCF calibrating what real bandwidth looks like.

Does the expectation affect the question? Yes, legitimately and already:""")

# ---- new §6.8 metals + conditions ----
sub("---\n\n## 7. The measured record",
"""### 6.8 The metals, the conditions, and the reconstruction

The crack of §6.6's fork now has names, from the measured record (searched and verified this session): the screening survey covered 58 samples; large effects in most metals, none in the noble metals Cu, Ag, Au, small (gaseous-level) effects in insulators, semiconductors, and lanthanides — the periodic table itself supplying the on/off pattern — and the enhancement *decreases with increasing temperature*, following the classical Debye model: the first observed temperature dependence of a nuclear cross section. The named cells: **tantalum, U_e = 309 ± 12 eV, verified and independently confirmed** — naive coordinate 11.4, above both the discovery floor (4.26) and the nominal watt threshold (10.5), with *no ambient precision-calorimetry archive pinning its real coordinate* — and **palladium, ~800 eV** *(survey value recalled; flag)*, naive coordinate ~30, whose own decades of μW-precision D₂ calorimetry bound its ambient d–d coordinate below ~6.2 (computed, A.9): the surviving Pd window is **m ∈ [4.26, 6.2]**, a band beneath every calorimeter ever pointed at the metal, uninspected on the γ observable in thirty-seven years because the corpus measured heat, and heat goes dark three coordinates above where the line lights up. (One computation-corrected near-error is registered at R18; one flag for Q: a 2025-era platform combining electrochemical loading with beam bombardment reports Pd and Ti hydride yields 10¹⁸ over bare rates — beam-driven, not ambient, but ⅅ_phys moving on this axis.)

The conditions for achievability from these metals, enumerated with numbers (A.9): **C0**, the master condition owned by nature — the beam screening must be *static*, shown to a thermal bound deuteron, quantitatively a screening length of **0.125 Å** at the site against the ~0.5 Å (≈ 29 eV) of degenerate Thomas–Fermi theory — the grid's first empty cell, measurable but not engineerable; **C1**, temperature, the one condition with a verified lever: required effective density falls linearly in T (9.1 × 10²¹ cm⁻³ at 300 K → 1.2 × 10²⁰ at 4 K), so a genuine effect must *grow on cooling*; **C2**, co-located H + D at measured high loading, held; **C3**, pair confinement — the calibration anchor is a 0.74 Å molecule, interstitial sites sit ~2.9 Å apart *(recalled; flag)*, and vacancy–hydrogen clusters are the engineering route *(recalled; flag)*; **C4**, cleanliness at theorem grade with the periodic table's verified null row in the same apparatus. The three invariants no condition can move: listed exits only, ash in the bracket, and the d–d γ prohibition at any loading, any temperature, any vacancy density — conditions move the rate, never the reaction's face.

The exact reconstruction is issued as the companion document ***The Tantalum Test*** (v0.1, rendered alongside this paper): Run 0 Au blank, Run 1 Ta, Run 2/2b Pd, three fills each, full temperature ladder, with two computed design facts that make it unusually decisive — **the first day decides** (a 1-day null already bounds U_e,amb(Ta) < 117 eV against the 309 eV beam value, and ninety days improves this only to 110), and **the cooldown is its own verdict** (if C0 holds at all at room temperature, Debye scaling predicts ~10⁸× by 77 K: the ramp detonates the signal or executes the map). Its expected result, at the grade that has never missed: the first ambient screening number tantalum will ever have.

---

## 7. The measured record""")

# ---- §8.2 the verdict ----
sub("In the form of the book's Chapter 13 — stated limits, not modesty:",
"""### 8.2 The verdict, stated plainly

Asked directly, the investigation answers directly, with the word split as the work split it. *Possible in principle:* yes, and measured — μCF runs literal cold fusion at ~10¹² s⁻¹; no theorem forbids the reaction cold, only prices it. *Achievable at ambient with ordinary electrons:* almost certainly no — the claim needs 32–51 orders of enhancement, the only measured point at the required coordinate used a particle 207× heavier than an electron, and the historical claimed version specifically is dead on the physics (an exact EM prohibition, a 10⁹-quantum price, and ash it cannot hide), not on the sociology. The entire residual possibility lives in one measured crack — the beam screening values of §6.8 — which is real, cheap to close, and the only place "yes" could live; the honest weight on it is low, and it is testable in months. *Describable if proven:* yes, completely, and in advance — the reaction has exactly one admissible face (§6.6's description, checked five independent theorem-grade ways by the Tantalum Test), because the index, conservation, and electromagnetism jointly leave it nowhere else to stand. The first claim is held at the grade that has never hit, the second at the grade that has never missed, and one cheap measurement stands between them.

In the form of the book's Chapter 13 — stated limits, not modesty:""")

# ---- Register R17, R18 ----
sub("*Caught by: the corpus harness, first run.*",
"""*Caught by: the corpus harness, first run.*

**R17 — operator-relativity of E; the criterion; ℛ's third limitation.** The decuplet computation (A.8) showed the same ten cells at E = 0 (SU(3) operator) and E = 6 (pairwise ℛ): E is a property of the pair (index, operator), and every E-statement now carries operator scope (§3.1). The pairwise operator's third registered limitation — sum-constraint blindness — completes the species: functional and linear dependences are invisible to pairwise maxima. The payment: the symmetry-protection criterion (§3.9), which resolves the paper's 0-for-9 against the Ω⁻'s 1-for-1 and grades every expectation in §6.7. *Caught by: computing the indicated third floor under both operators before writing either result (B.2.13/B.2.14; the commitment named both outcomes and held).*

**R18 — a near-error corrected by computation before print.** In deriving palladium's surviving window, the collaborator's mental arithmetic put the calorimetric bound at m < 2.8 — which would have closed the Pd crack entirely — and the computation returned m < 6.2, leaving the 4.26–6.2 band open. The error inverted the conclusion's sign for one metal and never reached a sentence, because the number was computed before the sentence was written. Recorded not as a defect of the paper but as a measured instance of B.2.14 doing the exact job it exists for. *Caught by: the rule, functioning.*""")
sub("Sixteen entries for one short paper.","Eighteen entries for one short paper.")

# ---- §9.5 ----
sub("The operational rule going forward, stated as the sheet states its constraint: **nothing ships before the corpus harness passes**, and MEASURE means measured.",
"""The operational rule going forward, stated as the sheet states its constraint: **nothing ships before the corpus harness passes**, and MEASURE means measured.

### 9.5 The fourth pass, against v0.7

Run after §§3.9, 5.6, 6.8, 8.2, the §3 restructuring, and Appendices A.8–A.9 entered by simultaneous entry, with the register at eighteen. The commitment named PROJECTION on the twelve new Appendix C rows as the at-risk cell. Results are recorded below this line only after the run; the corpus harness (both documents, both shipped PDFs, cross-document layer) gates the build as always. Outcome: entered post-run in this section by the same simultaneous-entry rule that R14 taught — no forward reference precedes its target.""")

# ---- Appendix A.8, A.9 ----
sub("**A.4 — Figures.**",
"""**A.8 — The decuplet, both operators.** Coordinates (n_d, n_s), n_u = 3 − n_d − n_s ≥ 0. Full decuplet: |X| = 10; pairwise ℛ: |ℛ| = 16, E = 6 (six non-particle cells admitted); SU(3) operator (completion to the multiplet simplex): E = 0. 1962 dataset (Ω⁻ unobserved): pairwise E = 3; SU(3) E = 1, hole = Ω⁻. Equal-spacing rule on occupied rows (Δ 1232, Σ* 1385, Ξ* 1533 MeV, recalled): gaps 153, 148 → predicted m(Ω⁻) = 1684 MeV; measured 1672 *(recalled)* — 0.7%.

**A.9 — Metals, bounds, conditions.** Naive coordinates: Ta 309/27 = 11.4; Pd 800/27 ≈ 29.6 *(Pd value flagged)*. Calorimetric ambient bounds for Pd (d–d, per mole-scale): no heat above 1 W → m < 9.6; 1 mW → 7.6; 1 μW (published precision) → **6.2**; surviving Pd window [4.26, 6.2]. C0 quantitative: U_e ≥ 115 eV ⇔ screening length ≤ 0.125 Å (e²/4πε₀ = 1.440 eV·nm); Debye density ladder for 115 eV: 9.1 × 10²¹ cm⁻³ (300 K), 2.3 × 10²¹ (77 K), 1.2 × 10²⁰ (4 K); Thomas–Fermi reference ~0.5 Å ≈ 29 eV. Tantalum Test sensitivity ladder (nominal ε = 10⁻², b = 0.05 c/s, 0.01 mol pairs): 1 d → U_e,amb < 117 eV; 30 d → 112; 90 d → 110; cooldown factor at m(295 K) = 4.5 under Debye: ~10⁸ by 77 K.

**A.4 — Figures.**""")

sub("12. Accelerator screening-potential measurements in deuterated metals (representative: Raiola et al., Eur. Phys. J. A, 2004 era, LUNA-adjacent programs) — the 100–800 eV range; *recalled attribution, listed with flag*.",
"""12. Accelerator screening-potential measurements in deuterated metals — the 100–800 eV range; superseded in specificity by refs. 13–14.

import re, math

eV=1.602176634e-19; NA=6.022e23
regs=re.findall(r"\*\*R(\d+) —",md); secs=re.findall(r"^## (\d)\.",md,re.M)
F.append(("19 SEQUENCE",secs==[str(i) for i in range(1,10)] and regs==[str(i) for i in range(1,19)],f"register {len(regs)}"))
# LATTICE incl. decuplet
full={(a,b) for a in range(4) for b in range(4) if a+b<=3}
A=[sorted({c[i] for c in full}) for i in (0,1)]
ph=lambda i,j,v: max((c[i] for c in full if c[j]<=v),default=-1)
Rp={(a,b) for a in A[0] for b in A[1] if a<=ph(0,1,b) and b<=ph(1,0,a)}
F.append(("1 LATTICE",len(Rp)-len(full)==6,"decuplet pairwise E=6 recomputed"))
# EQUATIONS: new numbers
chk={"1684":(1533+ (153+148)/2),"0.125":1.4400/115*10,"9.1":None,"117":None}
ok=abs((1533+150.5)-1684)<1.5 and abs(1.44/115*10-0.125)<0.002
G2p=145.2
r=5*math.sqrt(0.05/86400)/1e-2; lam=r/(0.01*NA); x=1-math.log(lam/1e-55)/G2p
ok = ok and abs(1/x**2-4.34)<0.03 and abs((1/x**2)*27-117)<1.5
n300=0.025852/((1.4400/115*1e-7/743)**2)
ok = ok and abs(n300/9.1e21-1)<0.03
F.append(("2 EQUATIONS",ok,"1684, 0.125 Å, 117 eV, 9.1e21 all reproduce"))
# ENUMERATION / CONSISTENCY / REDUNDANCY sweep
stale=[x for x in ["All three figures","Sixteen entries for one short paper","Fourteen entries","run against it three times"] if x in md]
F.append(("15 ENUMERATION","Eighteen entries" in md and len(regs)==18,"18 = Eighteen"))
F.append(("3 CONSISTENCY",not stale,f"stale: {stale}" if stale else "sweep clean"))
F.append(("4 REDUNDANCY",not stale,"summaries current"))
# ANTECEDENT (incl. no dangling §9.5-style forward refs: §9.5 exists)
heads=set(h.strip(". ") for h in re.findall(r"^###? (\d\.\d[\.\d]*|\d)\.? ",md,re.M))
refs=set(re.findall(r"§(\d\.\d)",md))-{"18.6","23.3","23.4","11.4","21.8","25.7","22.2","1.1","1.2","1.3","2.4","21.1"}
F.append(("11 ANTECEDENT",refs<=heads,f"unresolved {sorted(refs-heads)}"))
F.append(("12 MARKUP",md.count("**")%2==0,"balanced"))
# PROJECTION: new C rows present (the committed at-risk cell)
appC=md.split("## Appendix C")[1].split("## References")[0]
miss=[x for x in ["1684","0.125","117 / 112 / 110","[4.26, 6.2]","9.1×10²¹","52.0 fm","58 / Cu"] if x not in appC]
F.append(("20 PROJECTION",not miss,f"missing: {miss}" if miss else "all new numbers indexed"))
# SCOPE: E operator-scoping declaration present near definition
F.append(("10 SCOPE","E means E_ℛ" in md,"operator scope declared at §3.1"))
# ATTRIBUTION: refs 13-15 exist and are cited
refsec=md.split("## References")[1]
F.append(("7 ATTRIBUTION",all(k in refsec for k in ["Eur. Phys. J. A* 19","J. Phys. G* 31","Materials-driven"]),"refs 13–15 listed"))
for a,ok,d in F: print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL':4}  {a:14} {d}")
EOF

**The collapse relation.** Every cell of the nuclide chart is, opened up, an entire closed index one floor down — a nucleus is a bound configuration of the hadron index — and every element coordinate of Λ is a chart cell closed and collapsed: *an index below is a point above.* Two adjacent floors plus their bridge indicate a third by continuation, and the honest test of an indicated index is whether it exists and closes in ⅅ_phys. The ash bracket made the fourth channel unable to hide the nucleus; EM prices its ability to hide the energy. The verdict machine deliberately leans on neither. **(iii) The p + d ordering acquires a theorem.** Non-identical reactants open E1 at 226 fm — the least-mismatched radiation on the light chart — so the target cell is EM-permitted exactly where the historical channel is EM-forbidden, and the licensed channel donates a free discriminator: an E1 capture line carries a characteristic angular pattern (~sin²θ, ideal 90°/30° ratio 4.0 — *recalled; flag*), so a candidate 5.49 MeV line failing E1 systematics is artefact by selection rule.""")

The crack of §6.6's fork now has names, verified where possible. **Tantalum**: U_e = 309 ± 12 eV, measured and independently confirmed — naive coordinate 11.4, above both the discovery floor and the nominal watt threshold — and *no ambient precision archive exists for it*. **Palladium**: largest survey value (~800 eV, *recalled; flag*; naive coordinate ~30), the Fleischmann–Pons metal rediscovered anomalous by beam physics — but its own decades of μW calorimetry bound its ambient coordinate below ~6.2, leaving the window **m ∈ [4.26, 6.2]**: a band beneath every calorimeter ever pointed at it, uninspected in thirty-seven years because the corpus measured heat, and heat goes dark three coordinates above where the line lights up. 12:The question "can a stable cold fusion reaction be identified between two cells of Λ?" is put to the framework of *The Method* and answered by the framework's own machinery. The answer is a refusal, derived on three independent routes (B.2.8): by the law (E(Λ) = 0, §18.6 — a complete index makes exactly zero predictions), by the coordinates (all eight are electronic; the bracket is measurably blind to nuclear charge, Ch. 11), and by the data (ⅅ_phys terminates outside the index, and no reproducible measured levels exist to bracket). The refusal is then treated as P8 requires — as a bound, not a dead end. It identifies the correct index for the question: the nuclide chart on (Z, N), named in §1.2 of the book. Computed on measured particle-stability data rather than as drawn, that chart is **not** closed: E(X) = 9 on the window Z ≤ 9, and the nine cells the structure admits and nature denies are ⁵He, ⁷He, ¹⁰Li, ⁸Be, ¹³Be, ⁹B, ¹⁶B, ¹⁸B, and ²¹C. Seven of the nine have odd N — the pairing staggering the coordinates cannot carry; the two even-N exceptions carry their own physics: ⁸Be (even–even; alpha clustering) and ⁹B (odd-Z; the unpaired proton on the proton-rich side). The drawn chart is proved to be exactly the ℛ-closure of the measured one (idempotence verified; E(drawn) = 0), which corrects the referent of the book's §1.2 row and converts its E = 0 entry into a statement about a model band. Three of the nine holes — ⁵He, ⁸Be, ⁹B — are the compound systems of the classic two-cell fusion reactions, so the chart's non-closure *is* the reaction mechanism: fusion exit channels and missing cells coincide. Finally, the achievability question is reduced (P3, with its residue stated per B.2.16.3) to a laboratory commensurability protocol: per watt of claimed excess heat, 1.91×10¹² events/s through ³He + n, 1.55×10¹² through t + p, or 2.62×10¹¹ through ⁴He + γ, with heat and nuclear products required to agree through Q along two routes sharing no step. Null results are converted, per B.2.15, into upper bounds on the screened d–d rate enhancement — the claim under test being an enhancement of 51.5 orders of magnitude (computed) over the screened molecular baseline. The reduction makes the question decidable; it does not make the answer yes. Two further results complete the arc. First, the chart's closure is priced: fibred by N-parity, the odd-N fibre closes exactly (E = 0) and the even-N fibre carries E = 2, so one properly fibred coordinate buys seven of the nine holes — while the same coordinate naively appended explodes E to 94, a measured warning that E-statements are fibration-dependent — and the residual two cells, ⁸Be and ⁹B, are closed by no coordinate nature offers. Second, the only lattice-licensed route to a conditional prediction is constructed and instrumented: a screening bracket calibrated on two independent measured anchors agreeing to 2% across seventy-two orders of rate, which orders the search to p + d → ³He + γ, fixes the detectability coordinate at m\* = 4.26 ± 0.09 (≈ 115 eV under a flagged linear map), and — via a companion protocol and computation annex — reduces the laboratory question to a verdict machine whose only unfixed symbol is the outcome. The two commensurability identities are then unified into the investigation's sharpest single object: the **ash bracket** — every possible d–d branching, measured or invented, must deposit between 3.76 × 10⁻⁸ and 2.74 × 10⁻⁷ mol of heavy ash per watt-day, a window only 7.3× wide whose completeness is guaranteed by the chart's exhaustive exit enumeration rather than by any dynamical assumption, making "heat without commensurate ash" excluded by conservation itself and closing any specific claim with one measured point at 30% precision. Finally, the lattice's expected output of the test is derived and shown to be an expectation of form, not value — a coordinate per cell, unconditionally — which reshapes the question (a fork informative on both branches) while remaining structurally unable to touch the answer, by the commit-before-look mechanism built for exactly that severance. Three further arcs complete the work. The index tower: the collapse relation ("an index below is a point above") continues the two studied floors to a third — the hadron index — where the 1962 decuplet, computed here under both operators, carries physics' one successful hole-prediction (Ω⁻, E = 1 at exactly its cell, mass retro-predicted to 0.7%), yielding the criterion that resolves this paper's own 0-for-9: **holes predict if and only if their closure is symmetry-protected**, and E itself is operator-scoped. The electromagnetic layer: EM is the unique interaction with cells in both studied indexes, so every ambient claim is a claim about one bridge; the exit simplex is EM-pinned (s-wave d + d → ⁴He + γ is 0⁺ → 0⁺, an exact single-photon prohibition), the off-simplex channel is priced (~10⁹ coherent quanta across a 1,900× scale mismatch), and the same symmetry that forbids the historical channel licenses the target one. Finally the instrument is pointed: tantalum (beam U_e = 309 ± 12 eV, verified and independently confirmed; no ambient archive) and palladium (~800 eV, flagged; its own μW calorimetric history leaves the window 4.26 ≤ m ≤ 6.2 uninspected on this observable), with the noble metals as the periodic table's verified null row, the conditions C0–C4 quantified (screening length 0.125 Å required against Thomas–Fermi's ~0.5 Å; cryogenic density ladder computed), and the exact laboratory reconstruction issued as the companion *Tantalum Test* — where the first day decides the coordinate and the cooldown is itself a verdict. The paper closes with its own register of corrections, declines, and degraded provenance, and with the twenty prime audits of the companion method run against it three times, plus the standing corpus gate.
24:**The reduction.** The holes of the computed chart are the exit channels of real fusion. That fixes, per watt of any claimed excess heat, the nuclear product rates that must accompany it — three equalities that any calorimetry laboratory can test, under a protocol that is the book's Appendix B translated bench-ward (§§4–6). The measured record of thirty-seven years, including the ARPA-E program concluding in July 2026, is read against it (§7). What the reduction cannot do is stated in the book's Ch. 13 form (§8), and everything withdrawn, declined, or degraded in the course of this work is registered (§9).

two looked like one. The row now names the band, and the nine cells are recorded as what they are:
pairing and clustering, the terms the mass formula carries and the coordinates (Z, N) cannot.
Caught by computation, by the author, against a table that had stood since §1.2 was written.
299. A second named law, retained at §13.4.1: an open index does not close itself, except where
the closure operator is realised in the object's own structure. Half of it is trivial — sets do not
change — and the content is the exception: when an index closes, something in it is doing ℛ's work and
can be pointed at. Tested against every index this book indexes and holding on all ten: the box ordering,
the chessboard, Λ, the drawn nuclide band, the relabelled calendar all close and in each the realiser is
nameable; the printed calendar, the measured nuclide chart, the periodic table, unfibred Appendix E and

worth the size of its box. No precedent search has been run on it.

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"300. The twenty prime audits made executable and required on every output, at B.2.22. Until this entry
the audits were run by hand each session, which made audited a claim about a session rather than a
property of an artefact; they now live in a file that reads the source, the rendered PDF and the press by
name and exits with the count of failures. A build that has not been audited can no longer be
mistaken for one that has. First run: all twenty pass. Two limits are admitted rather than closed — the
script decides nothing, so every flag remains a hypothesis under B.2.19.7, four of the last five having
been detectors and not the book; and the script cannot audit itself, its own correctness being
untested by anything in the twenty. The three-hundredth entry of this register is a protocol that makes
the other three hundred and eighteen harder to repeat.
301. The caps printed in §3.3 do not reproduce Λ, and the construction is short an eighth condition. Both
were found by an outside paper — Indexing Electromagnetism, Lach and Claude, reconstructing Λ from
§2.1 alone — and both are reproduced here independently. The tuple (3,3,2,3) built literally yields
1,548 cells, not 976; only (3,3,1,3) with k ≥ 1 reproduces the object, and it reproduces every other
stated invariant at the same time. What located it was the coupling signature: drop the target's Pauli
bound g ≤ 2(2f+1) and 976 must become exactly 1,000, with the 24 excluded cells all at f = 0, g = 3 —
computed here at 1,000 and 24 with that signature exactly. And k ≥ 1 was never stated: with k = 0 the
tree collapses and twenty-five non-transitions survive, which §8.2's own words exclude and the
construction did not. A reader rebuilding from §2.1 and §3.3 as printed obtained a different
object, which is the most consequential defect this register carries. The paper reports 1,584 where this
recomputation gives 1,548; the disagreement is in the wrong figure and does not touch the correction.
302. The law of realised closure sharpened, at §13.4.1, into two modes. Λ closes by order — its tree of
monotone bounds is ℛ — and leaves nothing over. Maxwell's equations close by identity: ∇·(∇×H) = 0
turns pre-1861 Ampère's law into its own refutation, the repair is compelled, and the identity is the
realiser. Both satisfy the law as written and they deliver different things — the identity closed the
divergence part and left a free curl, closed afterwards and externally by covariance. Conjecture:
identity-realised closure leaves slack equal to the kernel of its realising identity;
order-realised closure leaves none. Two computed points, which is not a pattern. The law was stated
at register 299 with ten rows behind it and no distinction inside it; it now has one, and a falsifiable form.
303. A criterion this book had used without stating: an occupancy coordinate is admissible if and
only if its cap is a function of a single other coordinate. A multi-argument cap is a hyperedge and
costs meet-closure. Committed before computation and right in both directions — a rectangular cavity
mode index fails 768 meets in 15,400 pairs, a spherical one none in 114,960. §2.1 records that every
constraint of Λ is single-argument and that its graph is therefore a tree; it never said what the tree was

 The Method — The Lach Cylinder

113

buying. It was buying meet-closure, and the criterion is what makes Λ's shape a requirement rather
than a convenience.
304. The companion paper adds four elements to Appendix E and the index closes at forty, but the
consequence worth recording is which cell one of them fills. The slack = kernel conjecture is the
first element this book has ever carried at status conjectured. §E.2 defines five status values and
the enumeration had occupied three — proved, verified, measured — so a value the coordinate always
admitted had gone unused since the appendix was written. By register 275 that makes the zero stronger
and not weaker: a larger box, the same E. Appendix E was not survived by the paper; it was
improved by it, using a distinction the structure already carried and nothing had exercised. One value
is still unoccupied everywhere: cited. Every element of this index is checked rather than borrowed, so
§E.3's first constraint has never met an occupant to constrain.
306. The cap-arity criterion of register 303 is false in one direction, and applying it to chemistry refuted it

input.command:
cd /home/claude && python3 - << 'EOF'
h=open("audit_all.py").read()
old='''for val in ["1.136","8.8","32.5","4.26","3.76","309","5σ"]:
    present={n for n,d in [("paper",paper),("protocol",prot),("annex",ann),("tantalum-test",tt)] if val in d}
    vals_ok=True  # same literal string; disagreement would need differing digits
    rec("cross-doc","13 AGREEMENT",vals_ok,f"{val} in {sorted(present)}")'''
new='''# AGREEMENT with teeth (register 318): for each canonical quantity, any near-collision
# (same context pattern, different digits) in any document is a failure.
canon={"1.136":r"1\\.\\d{3} × 10¹²","32.5":r"3\\d\\.\\d orders","4.26":r"m\\\\?\\*?[_₍( ]*det[^=]*= ?\\d\\.\\d\\d|4\\.\\d\\d ±","309":r"30\\d ± 1\\d eV","3.76":r"3\\.\\d\\d × 10⁻⁸"}
docs=[("paper",paper),("protocol",prot),("annex",ann),("tantalum-test",tt)]
for val,pat in canon.items():
    bad=[]
    for n,d in docs:
        for mt in re.findall(pat,d):
            if val not in mt: bad.append((n,mt))
    rec("cross-doc","13 AGREEMENT",not bad,f"{val}: consistent wherever restated" if not bad else f"{val}: COLLISION {bad}")'''
assert old in h; h=h.replace(old,new)
open("audit_all.py","w").write(h); print("AGREEMENT rewritten with collision detection")
EOF
echo "=== fault injection round 2: must FAIL now ==="
